ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Light energy powers photosynthesis, which converts carbon dioxide and water into carbohydrates and what gaseous element?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a flowering plant, with blue flowers, green stems and leaves on the left, and roots extending into the soil/moisture area below. In the upper right there is the sun, and there is an arrow from the sun pointing to the plant; around the leaves there are also arrows indicating substances entering and leaving the leaves and letter labels. Reasoning: The question asks which gaseous element, along with carbohydrates, is produced when light energy drives photosynthesis, converting carbon dioxide and water. The standard photosynthesis reaction is carbon dioxide + water + light energy produces sugar/carbohydrates and oxygen. Therefore this gaseous element is oxygen.
